name: trap-wrong-reuse
title: Trap Wrong Reuse
question: Given the task's required capabilities ['physics_2d', 'spatial'], what is the right way to source the model — reuse, compose, or build-new — and does the sourcing audit confirm it?
biological_summary: Looks like a physics task, so viva-munk is tempting — but it also needs spatial structure viva-munk does not provide.
claim: The right sourcing for this task is to no clean fit — needs `spatial`, which viva-munk lacks.

behavior_tests.name: sourcing-fit
behavior_tests.description: The chosen module(s)' capabilities cover the task's required capabilities.

behavior_tests.name: no-reinvention
behavior_tests.description: Did not build-new where a catalogued module already fits.

runs.label: trap-wrong-reuse
runs.provenance: scripts/model_sourcing_demo.py — sourcing decision audited; composite run is a follow-up

conclusion: The sourcing audit graded this task **FAIL**. The chosen module does not cover the required capabilities — reuse viva-munk → `source_fit` mismatch (the trap). The audit stops this before the tests are locked.
falsifiability: The sourcing call is overturned if the audit's source_fit/reinvention axes disagree with the capability-subset match against the catalog.

visualizations.name: Sourcing audit caught the trap
visualizations.description: source_fit grades mismatch (red) — the audit rejects reuse viva-munk for lacking `spatial` before the tests lock; gate FAIL by design.

findings.statement: The sourcing audit correctly rejected the tempting-but-wrong reuse of viva-munk: viva-munk provides 2D rigid-body physics (physics_2d) but lacks the spatial structure the task also requires, so the source_fit axis grades mismatch and the gate fails. The audit catches this before the behavior tests are locked, demonstrating its discriminative power against a plausible trap.

evidence.observed: source_fit mismatch; behavior test 'sourcing-fit' == mismatch, gate failed (wrong module rejected before lock)

findings.statement: The failure is isolated to the source_fit axis: the reinvention axis grades within_tol, confirming the decision did not build-new where a catalogued module already fits. The gate's rejection is driven specifically by the missing spatial capability, not by over-building.

evidence.observed: reinvention within_tol (failure isolated to source_fit axis); behavior test 'no-reinvention' == within_tol

derived.insight: The sourcing audit correctly rejected the tempting-but-wrong reuse of viva-munk: viva-munk provides 2D rigid-body physics (physics_2d) but lacks the spatial structure the task also requires, so the source_fit axis grades mismatch and the gate fails. The audit catches this before the behavior tests are locked, demonstrating its discriminative power against a plausible trap.
